title: Microsoft SSO integration on macOS fails for SAML use cases
body:
User Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:133.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/133.0

Steps to reproduce:

1. Use Firefox on macOS
2. Have enterprise enabled MDM via Microsoft "Company Portal"; Device is "Compliant"
3. Enable "network.http.microsoft-entra-sso.enabled" in "about:config"
4. Visit some external web-application that is connected to Entra ID via SAML


Actual results:

1. There was a Microsoft login prompt
2. After providing login credentials, passing through MFA gate the message:

"You cannot access this right now"
"Your sign-in was successful but does not meet the criteria to access this resource. For example, you might be signing in from a browser, app, or location that is restricted by your admin."

is shown;

Under "More details", the "Device state: Unregistered" and "Device identifier: Not available" display, indicating that device compliance state was not passed to MS login page.


Expected results:

1. There shouldn't be a Microsoft login prompt (as there is SSO from computer's "Company Portal")
2. In any case, the login should have succeeded.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Latest revision now takes the `https://login.microsoft.com/` edge case into account, but now requires at least two `/` in path-query. Yes, currently the Entra SAML SSO POST's to `/XXX/saml2`, but say Microsoft changes it to plain `/saml2` (with `XXX` now going through the POST data) - the FF Entra SSO will break. Or say somebody visits `https://login.microsoft.com///` (3 slashes at the end) or `https://login.microsoft.com/#//` (2 slashes as part of a ref value) -- current logic would seemingly pass(?) SSO cookies.

Which brings us to the question - why is limitation on  `https://login.microsoft.com/` exclusion is needed at all? If I'm not mistaken, the Windows `#ifdef XP_WIN` part sends the SSO cookies to every page visit and doesn't even check for `isUriMSAuthority`. Why macOS SSO should be much more strict?

Isn't also such OS difference also a fingerprinting vector?  Would any privacy/"UA changer" extension be even able to see or intract with these SSO cookies?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
(In reply to comment #21)
> Latest revision now takes the `https://login.microsoft.com/` edge case into account, but now requires at least two `/` in path-query. Yes, currently the Entra SAML SSO POST's to `/XXX/saml2`, but say Microsoft changes it to plain `/saml2` (with `XXX` now going through the POST data) - the FF Entra SSO will break. Or say somebody visits `https://login.microsoft.com///` (3 slashes at the end) or `https://login.microsoft.com/#//` (2 slashes as part of a ref value) -- current logic would seemingly pass(?) SSO cookies.
> 
> Which brings us to the question - why is limitation on  `https://login.microsoft.com/` exclusion is needed at all? If I'm not mistaken, the Windows `#ifdef XP_WIN` part sends the SSO cookies to every page visit and doesn't even check for `isUriMSAuthority`. Why macOS SSO should be much more strict?
> 
> Isn't also such OS difference also a fingerprinting vector?  Would any privacy/"UA changer" extension be even able to see or intract with these SSO cookies?

SSO cookie parsing should not occur if we visit `https://login.microsoft.com` or `https://login.microsoft.com///` , we should get simply a [`didCompleteWithError`](https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/rev/48556b26b96a32672caa46b9abb6d56c234cd84f/netwerk/protocol/http/MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils.mm#201) from the API and then proceed with URI with query/path. Example:
```
[Parent 80503: Main Thread]: D/macOSSingleSignOn MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils::MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils()
[Parent 80503: Main Thread]: D/macOSSingleSignOn MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils::AddMicrosoftEntraSSO start
[Parent 80503: Main Thread]: D/macOSSingleSignOn MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils::AddMicrosoftEntraSSO [urispec=https://login.microsoft.com/]
[Parent 80503: Unnamed thread 171438f30]: D/macOSSingleSignOn SSORequestDelegate::didCompleteWithError: domain 'com.apple.AuthenticationServices.AuthorizationError' code -6000 (The operation couldn't be completed. (com.apple.AuthenticationServices.AuthorizationError error -6000.))
```

It should then redirect to a URI with appropriate query/path, at least based on testings. We just want to avoid going through unnecessary `MicrosoftEntraSSOUtils` run if the URI is empty, but I think this is a good point to consider.

comments.body:
Created attachment 9441711
Bug 1934271 - Remove GetQuery check in Entra SSO for SAML use cases


The [initial motivation](https://<redacted-host>/D216560#inline-1215772) behind checking whether the query is empty or not is to ensure that we don't perform SSO for URIs like `https://login.microsoft.com/`.

However, we observed that Entra SSO can operate via SAML using the URI `https://<redacted-host>/XXXXXX/saml2`.

To address this, we decided to remove the check like in Windows.

### beta Uplift Approval Request
- **User impact if declined**: macOS Users would not be able to complete Microsoft Entra SSO when the url involves SAML (e.g. https://<redacted-host>/XXXXXX/saml2).
- **Code covered by automated testing**: no
- **Fix verified in Nightly**: yes
- **Needs manual QE test**: no
- **Steps to reproduce for manual QE testing**: N/A
- **Risk associated with taking this patch**: No risk
- **Explanation of risk level**: This patch just enables SSO for all urls. If the url is invalid (e.g. `https://login.microsoft.com///`), we would receive a `didCompleteWithError `from the API and then proceed with URI with query/path
- **String changes made/needed**: N/A
- **Is Android affected?**: no
